paras: The Arcane Master is a powerful magic user that can cast multiple spells at once in a variety of ways, overwhelming opponents in a barrage of powerful magic.
The core of the Arcane master is on the multiple ways it can cast spells, be it with autospells, hard casts, quick casts, and any other method.
sections.title: Control of the elements

paras: The Arcane Master has no fixed rotation, since it's a spellcaster. It uses spells in a multitude of ways and can use autospell along with hard cast, which means:
It's a master of spells that can fight an enemy with full force and benefits, building small spells into larger, highly destructive spells.

As masters of the elements, they can take full advantage of the Elemental Focus system. Most of their spells are boosted by focus generated from thief level magic. A good Arcane Master will know to keep its focus stacks always maxed in order to deal the highest damage possible with its powerful magic.
With the situational use of Dual Cast, an Arcane Master can boost its overall damage in short bursts by managing its SP pool.
If the Arcane Master knows its limits, it can even hardcast very long spells while auto-attacking and causing spells to rain from both ways at once, since Dual Cast also affects autospell skills.

A good Arcane Master will have full use of the spells according to each situation, rotating them all while attacking to rain down autospell destruction... or standing far from enemies (thanks to Free Cast) and using its core spells to build the perfect Tetragrammaton for massive damage.
sections.title: Gameplay Identity

bullets: Comet changes elements according to the current weapon. It can also be affected by Double Cast.
The use of the 3 Thief spells (Flaming Petals, Freezing Spear, Wind Blade) and the Mystic spell Eruption is essential to properly manage elemental focus.
Unlimited Power can provide a boost to all damage needs, as long as SP is managed.
Magic Pierce from Assassin/Rogue can help decrease the issues of high MDEF targets.
Final Skill: Tetragrammaton. A targeted AoE that can be modulated into any combination of 4 hits with any element, according to the preparation.
paras: The Arcane Master has access to all Natural elements and a few others, which means it needs to adapt constantly to make full use of them:

With access to Mystic skills like Regenerate and Unholy Light, the Arcane Master can take more risks in small bursts, this ensures any player has a backup in case something goes wrong, as long as they correctly predicted it.
Managing skill costs and cast times is essential to any good Arcane Master, as casting a long spell at the wrong time can have terrible consequences or lead to loss of elemental focus stacks.

paras: The Black Plague is a job focused on applying different debilitations to an enemy, and using their applied statuses to boost the power of their other skills, alternatively, they can use sheer brute force to kill them with axe skills.
The Black Plague is a strong job when correctly used, and almost useless when not correctly built or played. It has important restrictions but these come with massive Pay-off.
sections.title: Death comes from inside

paras: The Black Plague has a variety of tools that can be used to massively boost the power of its skills, according to one's resources, time and skills, this makes them:
A very resistant debuff-stacker that can apply cumulative damage based on how much they debilitate their enemy with multiple burst window skills.
The Black Plague has many complex rotations. Most of the Axe-side of the tree is very simple to use, albeit with some HP costs and management buffs.

It's strongest potential comes on its poison skills. By applying it through many ways (Envenom, Enchant Poison, Venom Splasher...) one can stack a massive venomous bomb into an enemy, ready to be detonated with different means.

The Black Plague can also carry Toxins, specific items that can be applied anytime to improve their combat capacity and debuff enemies even further. They may also craft such toxins themselves, which might be preferable for long fights as the materials are much lighter than the toxins themselves.
NOTE: The Poison negative status and element have been reworked in Return to Morroc, allowing them to be useful and reliable. Check Stat Changes and Elemental Table for more details.
sections.title: Gameplay Identity

bullets: It's important to apply Poison status to targets to take full advantage of the kit.
Against poison-resistant enemies, the Axe skills are not only a backup plan but a very viable strategy.
Toxins are a strong buff/debuff at the same time, when correctly used, can make impossible situations easier to manage.
There are many ways to passively deal damage as a Black Plague.
Building a Black Plague is very complex and many skill can be used regardless of situation. It's important to find a healthy balance of offense and utility to ensure the effectiveness of the job.
Final Skill: Enchant Deadly Poison (Lv3). A powerful buff that increases the multiplying power of most offensive skills of the Black Plague, adding yet another bonus damage layer.
paras: The Black Plague can be a very complex job to manage. Due to the depth of its gameplay style, correctly playing a Black Plague can deal incredible damage and quickly assist any party members due to enemies being very debuffed:

Due to the large amount of tools to keep track of, it's important to elaborate the best way to apply all debuffs to a target, in a way you both have sufficient time to apply all of them, and to make use of them.

A simple example rotation: Apply poison status with Envenom, Increase poison element strenght with Venom Mark, debuff poison defenses with Death Cloud, deal massive damage with Venom Buster, which deals poison-element extra damage according to poison status and state of target. This can be further expanded with Enchant Deadly Poison, Toxins, Axe skills and many more.

paras: The Blast Juggler is a master of bombs and traps that can prepare the perfect ambush to enemies.

sections.title: Total control of the field

paras: The Blast Juggler can setup and prepare for any fight under the right terrain, ensuring enemies have a difficult time even before the fight starts, which:
Makes them masters of controlling the flow of battle, managing the movement and positioning of both the party and enemies.

The Blast Juggler's main feature is access to a multitude of Gadgets. These gadgets provide multiple ways for the player to interact with the enemies and their environment. The traps can be laid in a way that either protects the party or create a safe path to lure enemies to deal damage, or setup behind the party in order to create a safe escape route or avoid ambushes by causing status effects.

With the multiple status effects caused by the traps, along with their fixed damage, a good Blast Juggler can take full advantage of it to deal heavy damage with the Bomb skills, dealing bonus damage against enemies under specific effects. Rogue's Gadget Mastery is essential to setup traps from a safe range.

This doesn't mean the traps can't be used to handle monsters. Due to their special damage properties, they are reliable and predictable on their power, and Cluster Bomb is a specific trap for dealing heavy damage to enemies.
Blast juggler can also support their party members with equipment protection, cooking +10 stat food (which can't be traded, only thrown) and with improved potion healing effects.

paras: Cards were always a core part of the classic experience. As such, in Return to Morroc, we expect players to get any card they wish, as long as they can consistently handle its monsters. As a core experience, they are now essential to facing the hardest challenges, and as such, are a more attainable goal for any player prepared for the challenge.
Every card effect was completely remade from scratch. Some might even include new art (the ones that don't will be updated eventually).
We don't believe that killing something 10.000 times means its difficult to obtain. We believe that's a time sink.
We don't like time sinks. We value player experience and time.
This drop rate ensures cards are reasonable to farm and can be obtained eventually, if a player consistently can handle the monsters that drop those.
With the 100% remade effects, cards from Mini Bosses and MVPs no longer are an instant broken asset, but an interesting concept that can be built around.
sections.title: Reasonable Treasures

bullets: Renewal made equipment too strong with cards applying only to weapon/equip attack. This meant stats were mostly irrelevant.
Pre-Renewal had the opposite issue: card modifiers applied to all attack, making lower level weapons with more slots more useful.
Return to Morroc splits a card bonus between stats and equipment, 1/2 for each, this ensures the bonuses require a healthy balance between stats and equipment for ideal effect.
Note that left-hand weapons only receive 1/3 the bonuses, not 1/2.
Final Modifiers like Ranged Damage, Melee Damage and ATK+% are unchanged.
MATK bonuses are unchanged.
Keep in mind that a card that says +10% damage vs Fire for example also includes MAGIC and not only physical attacks.
paras: Return to Morroc aims to also rework bonuses that may be an issue in balancing the impact of both stats and equipment. We found a balance that strikes closer to our vision of card bonuses:
Card damage bonuses are split between stats and equipment. This means if you get, for example, a +10% vs Large Size card, you'll get a 5% bonus from your stats, and 5% from your equipment.
sections.title: A true balance of card modifiers

bullets: Some cards can now have multiple slots that they can fit. Like a card being a Garment or Shoes Card. allowing you to wear more than one copy, or matching combos in different ways.
Some cards may now have extra restrictive slots, such as being a Lower Headgear-only card. Usually these cards bear unique effects or are very powerful.

Finally, some simple cards can have a bonus that applies to Any Slot, allowing a player to stack as many of them as they want, in order to fully specialize a build around a concept, with expected downsides.
paras: Return to Morroc believes players should be able to customize their experience to their play style. so Cards now may have different use cases.
sections.title: Reworked Slots Systems

bullets: Some equipment may have extra slots, such as accessories with 2 slots, or similar effects.
Paradox equipment, that can be obtained in Varmundt's Mansion have 2 slots. They have negligible bonuses by themselves.

Sage equipment, that can be obtained in Dicastes Diel have 3 slots. These equipment require many Distortion Essences, items obtained from the Distortion Dungeons, and are a very good goal for end-game farming. They have very basic bonuses, but their versatility due to 3 slots is unmatched.

In Return to Morroc, facing monsters head-on and expecting to outstat them is a BIG problem. Monsters now have different interactions and behavior and they will cause problems if you just try to ignore them.
As a side note, this acts as a basic anti-bot system...because you WILL need to move out and react.

Using Heal Lv3+ is expected from all players. Not relying on potions and items to heal. For this reason it's strongly recommended to always have a Heal Manual of any capacity in hand to improve Heal Lv available and to get basic INT for good SP Regen and Heal Power.
It's recommended to check Stat Changes For more details on background changes.
If you approach the combat the same way you approach it on classic, you will struggle, a LOT.
sections.title: New Threats

bullets: This doesn't apply to bosses.
Some monsters may have their basic attacks as a mechanic itself, with quick or strong hits.
Lower fields and low rank dungeons usually have long cast times, lower damage and more margin for error.
Higher fields and higher rank dungeons usually have quick cast times, higher punishment for errors or straight up fail mechanics.
A Monster might use Revelation/Ruwatch on you to block your use of hiding to dodge targeted skills.
A Monster might use an AoE directly on you as a targeted skill instead of self to check your positioning and your party.

A Monster might use offensive skills that you need to take advantage of to prepare for the next action, like it creating a Safety Wall and a few seconds later instantly cast a heavy hitting melee skill.
paras: Monsters now deal very reduced auto attack damage. this is considered "Check" damage. if you can't survive this damage, it means you're not ready for this fight.
Monsters now cast skills very often.
Monsters may use skills in unexpected/forbidden ways.
All monsters can be killed with the approapriate gear. They might just need thinking about how to approach this situation.
sections.title: Monster AI Changes

bullets: Regular monsters fight with direct skills and behavior. They are the common monsters found everywhere.
Champion monsters are stronger than the other monsters of the same area and require attention to fight. They usually provide much higher EXP than usual.
Mini-Bosses are strong monsters that usually have weaker variations of MVP's mechanics, they are a good practice method, when available, before taking on a MVP.

MVP Bosses hit hard and have aggressive patterns, they may have specific punishment and counter skills to common tricks, They may have long casts for simple skills denoting it's not time to run, but to take advantage of it. Most MVPs don't resummon slaves, and some don't have any of them. They may also change behaviour when their HP get lower.
Some monsters might always come in pairs or summon other unique monsters when a certain condition is met. This is very relevant for creating specific conditions, including Dracomancer's job quest.
sections.title: Monster Group Changes

bullets: Targeted Cast: Just hide or break sight line. You can also silence or stun the target.
Untargeted Cast: Usually means an AoE around self or specific skill. move away just in case.
Small circle ground Cast: Usually means a directional skill, move out of that direction.
Large circle ground Cast: A Large AoE on the shown Area.
Red Squares around caster: A strong skill with unique properties. Move out.
paras: It all depends on four factors.
1- The Enemy is a Boss. In this case, you can't directly hide from it's skills. You'll need to either survive targeted skills or find barriers/break sight line.
2- The Enemy is a Demon or Insect. In this case you can use the same strategy as bosses or wear equipment/cards that grant you perfect hiding.
3- The Enemy is anything else. Regular fightning mechanics apply.

4- The Enemy is using a special skill in an unexpected way (usually only in Rank S dungeons), the skill cannot be avoided and must be handled indirectly such as by failing a skill dodge on purpose, swapping gear or other ways.
Some Skill Types:
Keep in mind some monsters are immune to Silence or Stun due to high status.
NOTE: It may be also a valid strategy to knockback monsters so their AoE around themselves don't hit you or your party.
sections.title: Basic Combat Mechanics

paras: In Return to Morroc, spamming a single skill over and over is the least efficient way to play (Unless you're a Jester, of course.), multiple cooldowns, costs, variations and combo interactions exist.
There are multiple ways skills can interact with one another to enable combos.
sections.title: New Powers

bullets: Combo Ready skills are skills that can be used without an opener, but they have diminished effects.
These skills can have either situational or direct requirements.
Combo Ready status lasts for a few seconds depending on the job class/skill used. Some Openers in this case allows up to 2 skills to be used if the After-Cast Delay is fast enough.
ANY Opener skill can be used to trigger the combo ready status. That means if a job has 2 different openers, any of them can be used to use the follow-up skills.
Revenant's Roaring Overslash deals extra 10% +1% per LUK damage if used during Combo Ready, You can get Combo Ready with both Scythe Reap (From Trickster) or from Reaping Slash.

Raider/Dracomancer's Spears Innate Fixed Bonus is Dragon Thrust. It enables Combo Ready by a few seconds, allowing the other skills from those jobs (like Heavy Stab or Crescent Dive) to deal full damage.
Jester's First Hand lasts enough for up to 3 skills according to ASPD/Delay of the user, many skills require it to deal full damage.

bullets: Shadowseer has this as a class mechanic, as most of their buffs have very long but mostly variable cast times. Their core skill, Equinox, grants Cast Ready for a short duration so they can quickly cast follow-up skills after it.
Some items grant Cast Ready when specific conditions are met, enabling quicker casting.
paras: Cast Ready reduces the variable cast time of skills by 95% for duration. This enables some skills to be used much faster under specific cases.
sections.title: Cast Ready

bullets: Stances usually don't have a fixed duration, and are used to change the combat flow for a job directly.
Stances have bonuses associated when they are turned on. They may also have downsides.
Deadeye's Headshot deals 1/10 damage if the user is not in Sniper's Nest stance. This stance massively reduces movement speed, while boosting final attack damage for all attacks.
Satsujin's Darkness Rises causes Satsujin's Curse status to all targets, other Satsujin skills deal extra damage against enemies afflicted by it.

Dracomancer's Dragon Force and Dragon Pact enable different skills to be used. Dragon Force allows use of the strongest spear skills, while Dragon Pact allows use of the draconic skills from the tree.

Duelist's Duel Stance increases defensive capabilities while allowing hits received to be stacked as Duel Counters. These counters can be used to deal direct damage to an enemy the more counters the character has.

Assassin's Fury Status boosts critical rate while enabling use of Executioner(and Gravekeeper) class skills. It has a fixed duration and Alpha, Omega, Cursed Coffin and Desolated Burial all require fury status. Gravekeepers have a secondary skill that allows then to enter fury status anytime with little restrictions.

Judge's Absolution, it's core skill, deals extra normal hits quickly against an enemy and needs a "Double Attack" proc from the passive Akimbo Mastery to be used. The skill also deals more hits according to skill level and current job level of the user. Violent Barrage also has the same requirement.

Thief's Cross Ripper Slasher can only be used if you have rolling counters, acquired from using Rolling Cutter and not moving. It also deals higher damage according to the current amount of counters, up to 3.

Executioner and Gravekeeper's Executioner Skills must be used one after the other in a specific order, with the last hit either being Cursed Coffin or Desolated Burial, both dealing critical chance damage, one being AoE and the other hitting harder.

sections.title: Direct Combo

bullets: There are no restrictions or requirements for using any of these, they also have no direct bonuses.
These combos can be hard to pull-off without practice or management of resources.
Use Illusion of Mist to cause Crystallize status.
Real Magic Attack and Illusion of Vermillion deal bonus damage vs Crystallize targets.
Use Illusion of Healing on target to reverse healing effects used on it.
Use Heal Lv10 with a manual along with healing power gear to kill the enemy with pure heal damage.
Apply Venom Mark to enemy, improving poison element damage they receive.
Apply Poison Status with Envenom, Venom Splasher, Enchant Poison...
Use Death Cloud to cause Inner Poison status, improving all poison damage further.
Use Venom Buster to deal poison elemental damage, with a double modifier if target is poisoned, while dealing extra damage due to Venom Mark and Inner Poison Status
Note: This combo doesn't work vs bosses due to their immunity to poison. They however can still receive Venom Mark.
Prepare a ton of SP with either SP cost reduction, SP regen, or SP refill stuff.
Get all coins from Coin Flip as needed and refill them as needed.
Activate Sniper's Nest to improve final damage.
Activate Ready to Rip to boost attack % power.
Activate Inquisition Resolve to add a chance for auto attacks to deal up to 6 hits.
Activate Killer Instinct for bonus status and flat ATK.
Activate Last Inquisition for ranged damage modifier bonus.
Activate Final Arrow to stack all the bonuses and modifiers on a single auto attack. This bonus is lost if you get hit or any of the previous buffs run out.
Auto attack an enemy to deal massive damage. Due to Inquisition Resolve, this bonus can hit up to 6 times (at a very low chance).
This is one of the highest damage dealing hits in the game.
Note: This combo can be used in smaller sizes and variety according to ease, logic and preparation.

paras: Dark Knight Requires Base Level 15 and Job Level 10 to start the quest.
The Dark Knight has the highest damage potential among all other job classes. The risk it requires taking to fulfill this, however, cannot be ignored by the player.
Its rotations are based on correct management and attention to risks of the class.
sections.title: Reversal of Curses

paras: The Dark Knight will always be risking its health in order to further boost its damage, making it:
A powerful warrior that will fight under a specific set of rules in order to extract the most out of its own risk as pure damage.
Due to its constant lack of HP, a good Dark Knight is required to be well aware of the damage potential of its targets. It should not be mistaken for a tank, but instead, acts as a pure DPS machine.
A higher level Dark Knight has access to Black Heart, which allows it to guarantee leeching damage dealt in order to continue on the offensive regardless of the situation.
sections.title: Gameplay Identity

paras: The use of Vengeance as a key opener is essential to deal constant damage. Some situations may not even require using any of the follow-up skills possible.
The great crowd control of Chilling Frost, which deals physical damage, makes it a reliable tool to control the situation of the fight due to its quick use and massive freeze chance.

The key feature of an offensive Dark Knight is Harvest, a stance that blocks most healing to a dark knight, but allows its missing HP bonus damage to reach the highest potential, by turning the fight into a kill or be killed situation. Harvest is a strong stance that requires running risks greater than any other job in the game, with incredible pay-off.

The Dark Knight has multiple tools to freeze, manage, and move around the fight while dealing heavy damage, correct analysis of the risk is essential to ensure the correct skill can deal massive damage, unlike any other job class.

paras: Distortion Dungeons are unique dungeons that require precise gameplay while under new rules.
The biggest difference for those is that each one has a unique mechanic, either simple or complex and take place in a different time period/timeline.
Distortions are either in the Past or in the Future, and when entering one, it tells you how far from the original timeline it takes place.
They are also always Rank B or higher.
sections.title: A challenge for the strongest

paras: The Dungeons require a powered-up Bifrost Mirror, each type of dungeon requires a a different level of it. The Bifrost Mirror has 4 levels of energy, depending on the current eyes slotted into it.
You can find the location of all pieces and details about them on the page linked above.
Reminder that Bifrost Mirror and the 4 Eyes cannot be stored or traded and are character bound.
Eye of Vidar: Travel to the past.
Eye of Vali: Travel to the future.
Eye of Thor: Travel to an alternate timeline or travel deeper within a distortion.
Eye of Balder: Travel to a paradox or world-ending event.
The Eyes can be added to the Mirror in Dicastes Diel (Sage's Palace). Once obtained, they are never lost and access to distortions is permanent and unrestricted.
sections.title: How to access a Distortion Dungeon

paras: Distortions may feature different rules and mechanics in specific cases, such as movement changes or buffs/debuffs.

A strong Dracomancer will find ways to change between stances as needed and using its large arsenal of defensive skills to fight any enemy.

In Return to Morroc, elements have an impact on the gameplay but no longer are the make or break they once were. The entire elemental table was changed.
The workings of elemental damage for physical attacks (both melee and ranged) is completely changed in place of a fixed modifier, regardless of monster level.
The elements are reworked into 3 groups: Corporal Elements, Natural Elements and Special Elements
sections.title: Elements Reworked

bullets: Seven Winds, Shinobi Skill, allows choosing between any non-neutral element except poison.
Enchant Poison, Thief Skill, allows enchanting weapon with poison element and a chance to cause poison status.
Burning Scythe, Trickster Skill, enchants the scythe with fire element and boosts fire magic power.
In case any of these skills is used, all damage will be converted to the element, including statusATK and WeaponATK.
You can also get elemental bonuses from some skills, such as Reaper Form making your damage Dark, or Dracomancer's dragon breath changing according to current buff activated.
paras: Return to Morroc has very few endow skills:
The only ways other than this to get full elemental benefits is either with elemental weapons/ammo or the Elemental Focus.
sections.title: Endow Skills

bullets: Skills that generate focus have increasing cast times and cooldowns with higher level, but generate more stacks. Using lower level skills won't increase the stacks past their current skill level.
Some Skills are boosted according to the current focus element and stacks amount.
Autospell does generate stacks, either from items or skills.
Casts Lv 10 Flaming Petals, generates 10 Fire Focus.
Casting Lv5 Flaming Petals will renew the duration of 5 Fire Focus stacks, the remaining 5 will vanish when the timer is up.
This can be repeated, so Spamming lower level magic after generating the Lv10 Focus to keep it up is a viable strategy.
A good magic user will know to not drop the stacks after they are obtained by keeping the offensive and weaving different spells into the rotation.
They get endowed with that element for duration, with full bonuses and penalties.
They deal 10% bonus damage vs the target advantage element (Like Water Focus vs Fire Enemy, you deal 10% extra damage).
This makes some physical builds weaving magic, even if only for the endow, a viable strategy in some cases.
paras: Elemental Focus is a sub-system of the magic of Return to Morroc. Natural element magic (Fire/Water/Earth/Wind) can generate or consume Focus for their element.
The Stacks can be seen as elemental icons around the player.
Focus duration is 60 seconds. Using lower level magic can refresh an amount of stacks equal to that point, for example:
When a Player has 10 Stacks, they get a bonus besides skills interactions:
Some unique skills (such as Mystic's Unholy Light) can get unique interactions according to the amount of element focus of the player.
Using a spell of a different element will change the focus to that element, losing any stacks of the previous element.
sections.title: Elemental Focus

paras: Elements apply to final damage. If a target is Fire Lv2 for example, it'll receive 125% damage from any source.
Contrary to Renewal, Elemental endows apply to the entire attack damage on Return to Morroc, not just to weaponATK.
sections.title: Elemental Modifiers

paras: Damage bonus/penalty according to elements has been changed.
Instead of varied amounts of bonuses vs elements, they have fixed amounts up to Lv3.
Lv4 monsters require specific approaches to fight, specially if they are Holy/Dark.
sections.title: Element Levels

bullets: Neutral has no interaction with Undead, is weak vs Ghost and Poison. Neutral has no bonus damage vs anything.
Poison is strong vs Neutral, weak vs Ghost and Undead.
Ghost is opposed to Undead, meaning both are strong vs each other. Also is strong vs Poison and Neutral.
Undead is opposed to Ghost, meaning both are strong vs each other. Also is strong vs Poison.
paras: The 4 Corporal Elements are: Neutral, Ghost, Undead and Poison.
sections.title: Corporal Elements

bullets: Fire is strong vs Earth and weak vs Water. No interaction with Wind.
Water is strong vs Fire and weak vs Wind. No interaction with Earth.
Wind is strong vs Water and weak vs Earth. No interaction with Fire.
Earth is strong vs Wind and weak vs Fire. No interaction with Water.
paras: The 4 Natural Elements are: Fire, Water, Wind and Earth.
sections.title: Natural Elements

bullets: Special Elements have a unique interaction with other elements:
Holy is strong vs all 4 Corporal Elements(Neutral,Poison,Ghost,Undead). It has 10% extra damage and 10% extra resistance vs them, regardless of Level.
Dark is strong vs all 4 Natural Elements(Fire,Water,Wind,Earth). It has 10% extra damage and 10% extra resistance vs them, regardless of Level.
Holy and Dark are opposed to each other. They have regular damage bonus and resistance vs each other, like other elements.
paras: The 2 Special Elements are: Holy and Dark.
sections.title: Special Elements

paras: Strongest Defensive Choice: Use same element as the attack received. If not available, use element strong vs attack received to mitigate damage.
Strongest Offensive Choice: Use element that is directly stronger vs enemy element for bonus damage.
Best Overall Use: Use holy vs corporal elements, use dark vs natural elements.

paras: The Gravekeeper is a powerful fighter that can quickly end battles with short bursts of critical damage. As an alternative, they can also quickly barrage their opponents with many quick attacks.
The core of their combat is around the way they can combo and simply ignore enemy defenses and resistances, making them always easy prey.
sections.title: Resources should be spent

paras: The Gravekeeper has a strong focus on chaining skills together to find an outcome, while debilitating enemies by decreasing their defenses, this makes them:
A heavy-duty job that can hit enemies with massive damage, while ignoring most defensive tactics used by them, ensuring they don't need to adapt much.
Since most Gravekeeper skills can crit, they have a very high power in dealing with enemies over both short and long fights, as long as their resources aren't drained.
The access to 2 different ways of achieving Fury status, with the Assassin's Fury and their own Loki's Fury provides them tools to always keep the aggression up.
The Gravekeeper has a short 3-skill combo where the last hit can be changed between a strong direct hit or an AoE to help with quick crowd-control and adaptation.

Gravekeepers also have access to a multitude of terrain and enemy debilitation by making them unable to fight effectively, either by revealing hidden enemies, petrification, large area coverage, doubling damage taken or straight up defense piercing, up to a point, as long as resources are available.
sections.title: Gameplay Identity

bullets: When using combos, always starts by casting Executioner's Alpha and Omega.
The final hit comes with either Desolated Burial or Cursed Coffin.
Making use of Cross Impact to fill in rotations with a very quick hit is a good way to extract extra DPS.
It's important to properly build a SP reserve due to the constant cost of the skill chains.
All builds should consider Loki's Mark for support and burst potential by doubling the enemy damage taken on next hit (Lex Aterna effect).
Final Skill: Mass Grave. A walking large AoE that deals massive physical damage to enemies caught in the path.
paras: The Gravekeeper is a job that only needs access to part of its kit, depending on how it's built by the player. It has different focus for different ways of fighting:

Due to the need to be in Fury status for its combo, the Gravekeeper needs to properly prepare how to achieve this status. Loki's Fury requires a large amount of SP but provides the status for a long time, being more recommended before engaging in combat, while Fury itself (from the Assassin tree) is a good way to keep it up later on. The Gravekeeper can also forego its combo skills entirely and focus on alternating Sonic Blows, Cross Impact, Impact Tooth and Fissure Tooth to overwhelm enemies with skill casts.

Gravekeeper is a job that values quick reactions and high skill use, the rotations outside of combo are very free form but require extra care on SP management to not burn it entirely and be exposed. The fact it can deal critical damage in many skills makes it a perfect user of Katar weapons.

The Illusionist is a unique combat where it has control of the Puppet, Kimi. The puppet can fight directly against enemies while the Illusionist stays on the sidelines providing support.

sections.title: Memories as weapons

paras: The Illusionist is played mostly as a support for the puppet, both with healing and control, along with direct damage, when playing:
Feels like controlling 2 characters at once, one with the focus on direct combat and another being supportive on the sides, require excelent micro-management.
The Illusionist can acquire a secondary weapon for free in Lutie. This weapon allows improved potential of support for Kimi and other players by improving healing power and pitching of items.
The Illusionist however will need to also fight and sometimes, deal most damage to generate Condensed Souls, essential for the growth of the Puppet and further on, for Grand Summoning.

Most of the Illusionist's offensive capabilities revolve around its core offensive skill, Real Magic Attack, a Good illusionist will mix both hardcasting the skill from a safe distance, or using the powers from the illusion glove along with a very high autospell chance to ensure it's applied constantly to enemies when safe.

A good Illusionist will know when to use its support skills, either by changing places with the Puppet or enemies using Master Swap and Illusion of Exchange, applying debuffs or covering an area with minor AoE skills to control any mobs that may show up.

The first priority should be to always keep the Kimi, the Puppet safe, as not having a Puppet in most cases and builds, may mean instant death. It's important to keep an eye on while reviving the puppet as even with no intimacy penalties, the SP cost can be a problem.

There are 4 types of Puppets, each with their own balance. A player can reroll their kimi by deleting the previous one(on the stats window) and summoning it again, keep in mind this will reset the level of the Puppet back to 1:
Agile Kimi Aggressive by default, has low defenses and sp growth, but high flee and attack speed. Excelent for low-management builds and focus.
Raging Kimi Aggressive by default, has balanced status overall with a focus on offenses. Very good for physical skill use and barrage of offensive skills.
Occult Kimi Passive by default, has high SP and magic growth, being very good for healing and magic casting. Better choice for players confortable with it.
Ward Kimi Passive by default, has high defenses and HP, an ideal choice for beginners or Illusionists who focus on support a pure damage while kimi tanks hits.

Jesters are medium ranged card fighters that deal quick and constant damage while burning through their huge SP pool.
The Jester core-mechanic is weapon swapping, as it can't recover SP naturally while fighting with Deck cards, needing to swap into a Shuffling Deck to recover SP in many different ways.

paras: Allows the use of spells, being the damage dealing card. They have an innate sp reduction passive, but also lock you out of natural SP regeneration.

♣ Clubs (Physical Attack): for physical builds, provides a great amount of ATK and bonus for skills such as First Hand .
♥ Hearts (Magic Attack): for magical builds, provides a great amount of MATK and bonus for skills such as Instant Aces .

sections.title: Path of the Orphan

bullets: The Thief is the "main" progress route for most players. It provides balanced gameplay with a large variety of choices.
The Thief tree is for players who are ready to fight and fulfill their destiny as an Orphan.
Thief, Assassin and Rogue can also UNCHAIN their jobs, locking them out of job changes, but unlocking new, mixed skill trees.
Reach Job Level 10 as Orphan.
Change into Thief.
Reach job Level 50 as a Thief.
Change into either Assassin(Path of Tradition) or Rogue(Path of Change).
Get Job Level 50 as Assassin or Rogue.
Choose one of the Specializations. This will unlock the Job Level cap from 50 to 70.
Get Job Level 70 with the Specialization. Specializations start at Job Level 50.
Change into final job Class. Max Job level is 70.
There are 8 possible final jobs: Night Raven, Satsujin, Black Plague and Gravekeeper for Assassin. Arcane Master, Kingslayer, Sinner and Blast Juggler for Rogue.
Thieves also have an unique alternative of abandoning the path and becoming Prowlers or Shadowseers.

bullets: The Trickster and the Vagabond are an alternative progress path for players. They provide unique mechanics and gameplay choices unlike any other.

Peacekeepers are a job from the new Frontier region, they fight using whips and trinkets.
Judges are the only job who can access the Inner Prontera Castle Headquarters.
Dark Knights focus on missing HP to increase the final damage of their skills.

Judge.best: Massive damage potential, High mobility and range, very quick SP regen.

paras: Judge Requires Base Level 15 and Job Level 10 to start the quest.
For Details about the main HQ and unique world interactions of judges, check the Judge Headquarters page.
The Judge has powerful combat potential by using revolvers. A good Judge on the battlefield is a game changer, a bad judge is nothing but a waste.
It's rotations are based on very defined preparation and burst phases.
sections.title: Swift Justice

paras: The Judge has a high damage potential, with an extra resource management in the way of the Seals, this makes the Judge:
An intense management job with multiple layers of preparation that grows exponentially according to its action flow.

Due to its very small SP pool, the Judge can't just mindslessly spam all its skills at once and hope for success, it needs a balanced flow of preparing it's seals (required for most of its skills), and using them to attack enemies.

On the other hand the Judge has very fast SP regeneration with its revolvers, when it has control of how to use its small reserve, they can shine and quickly flow from preparing their seals and bursting down enemies quickly.
sections.title: Gameplay Identity

paras: The Judge's main offensive tool is Absolution a powerful skill that can only be used after a double attack proc (usually from Akimbo Mastery).
Due to this, a good Judge will have decent ASPD, increase the double attack rate as much as possible to make it reliable and use the seals according to the situation needed.
Some of the skills from a Judge interact in many ways with its Job Levels, in the case of Absolution, the number of hits increases both with skill level and job level.
Due to its high scaling potential and unique weapons, the Judge is a job that has a very complex start, but once mastered, can dash in and out of combat in great flow.
As a final note, Magister Eye applies a mark to enemies, allowing any Absolution procs to hit multiple enemies anywhere on the screen and deal 1 extra hit.

Kingslayer.best: Highest HP, very defensive, great control with offensive skills.

paras: The Kingslayer is a tanky wall that can control and buff the party in a multitude of defensive ways.
Since they can take a lot of damage before going down, Kingslayers are a very strong choice for people looking for more survival or to take extra risks against enemies.
sections.title: Heart of the Party

paras: The Kingslayer doesn't have rotations, instead favoring the use of conditional skills, offensively and defensively to adapt to circumstances, so they are:
The core pillar of parties, who can change the flow of the gameplay directly, either by saving them from difficult moments or by increasing the margin for risks.

They are a unique class in regards to the skills distribution, since they are themed around Chess. This can be an issue due to the huge amount of skills they have at their disposal, making them unreliable in the hands of a player that doesn't know what to focus on. Regardless of skill levels, even a lower level skill can be very well used by a skilled player.

A Kingslayer, even if undergeared, can tank many hits due to its multiple mitigation tools, and if built around using a bow, they can use the rogue skill Cover in a much more similar way to the classic Paladin's Devotion by standing in the backline. (Devotion being a long term buff you can apply to many members, while cover lasts a few seconds but has a shorter range and no cast time, making it very good for quick saves and bursts of risky plays).
The Kingslayer can also attempt to quickly finish-off an enemy by casting Check Mate, dealing potential high damage if the resources are being well managed.
sections.title: Gameplay Identity

bullets: White Skills are focused on protection, defense, regeneration and mitigation.
Black Skills are focused on damage, control, knockback and monster interactions.
The 2 Gambit Skills (Queen and King) provide strong opportunities to handle a difficult situation, either by dealing high damage or quickly blocking a strong spell.
Final Skill: Check Mate. Converts the current SP amount into ATK% to deal damage to an enemy. The higher the SP, the higher total damage.

bullets: Shadow System: Dying in a dungeon is always tense, dying brings a Shadow to life that will try to kill your party members...But can also resurrect you if they are brave and fight back!
Skill based combat: SP Regen speed is drastically increased, SP is no longer a resource you exhaust and wait: it's something you control the constant use.
Combo Skills: Some skills now have special interactions when used right after another different skill. This can be extra hits or increased damage.
Skill Rotations: Skills no longer are spammed (with exceptions) and require rotating different cooldowns and skills in order to get maximum efficiency.

Monster Mechanics: You are required to dodge the skills used by monsters, or take a heavy hit. Move away from cast area, hide from targeted hits, run behind cover, dynamic combat situations with monsters who might assist one another, trap you with a curved ice wall, lock you in place or punish heavy mobbing overall.
Massively decreased numbers. Gone are the days of the barrage of 100k+ hits of renewal. Gone are the cheap one shot mechanics of MVPs.
Ranking System: Dungeons have difficulty tiers with differences based on what to expect, from E to S. Anything can be done solo with enough preparation and equipment.
Small bonus experience for fighting monsters above your level. Harsh penalties for monsters under your level, moving on and seeking new challenges is always needed.

paras: Mimic Requires Base Level 25 and Job Level 10 to start the "quest". Just check your reflection in the Orphanage Kitchen.

The Mimic is a unique job in the way that it doesn't have many unique tools to fight. It relies on copying other job skills and managing its cooldowns in order to attempt something semi-reliable. There are multiple ways a Mimic can manipulate its current skill poll, to some extent.
Its rotations are based on whatever the player wishes.
sections.title: Original while Plagiarizing

paras: The Mimic is a unique job that can copy other jobs in combat to varying degrees of success, this makes them:
A wildcard job with a lot of RNG choices and unpredictable behavior. While the player can influence what skills are used, It's almost never a safe bet.

The Mimic uses the Codex as weapons that can ignore any requirements for its plagiarized or Abracadabra skills. This means with some preparation, the Mimic can use extremely expensive skills for free, at the cost of its overall reliability.
As a side note, Mimics have terrible ASPD penalties while wearing a shield and any skill they cast has 1 second extra cooldown.
sections.title: Gameplay Identity

paras: Mimics have a core opener in their unique damage skill: Originality. This skill allows the mimic to deal reasonable damage on a lenghty cooldown, while activating both combo ready(to boost some skills) and cast ready(reduces variable cast time by 95%) for 10 seconds. This guarantees any eventual skills uses for follow-up will have high potential and efficiency.
The Mimic can also use the skill Tarot card of Fate to apply damage or random penalties/bonuses to enemies.
However, the core skills of the Mimic are Abracadabra and Plagiarism.
sections.title: Core Gameplay

paras: Abracadabra contains a random assortment of over 150 skills possible. Each level usually FAVORS the use of a specific skill type. While it doesn't guarantee, the chance is at least 90% of getting a skill of the type the player wants.
For example, using Lv2 Abracadabra will randomly cast an ATK-based skill, with single target nature 90% of the time, and the remaining 10% will be a random skill among all others.
Abracadabra also randomly changes if a skill is cast from afar or from close range.
Lv10 Abracadabra has a much lower cooldown ,but includes all skills at once, including a few exclusive ones.
sections.title: Abracadabra

paras: Being the other core skill of the mimic, along with Memorize (which locks the current learned skill), the Mimic can learn a massive amount of skills and use them in their own way.

The main ways a player can copy skills are by reading the Cantrip Books, books that players can find around the world that contain a set list of skills written on them (Allowing the Mimic to instantly copy any skill on the books, given they have the appropriate Cantrip Mastery level.).
They can also learn any "Player-skill-tree" skill directly from enemies by being hit with them and surviving the hit.
Cantrip Books always teach max level skills, while being hit is limited by the skill cast level. Regardless of this, It can never exceed Plagiarism's learned level.
At the end of the day, the core feature of a Mimic is being a job that allows plenty of fun options, while breaking the usual limitations of the game.

paras: Upon finishing tutorial you will be either 4/2 base/job level or 6/2 base/job level, based on rates chosen. You should get all basic stats VIT/DEX/INT to 10. then proceed on leveling main damaging stat to 30. Don't forget to put points into VIT/INT for max HP/SP and SP regen, and DEX for HIT if you miss a lot.
You can go down to Morroc Basement to get early levels for job change. While killing monsters in basement you can get your first normal gear and shadow set.
Level here until you get 10/10[Normal Jobs] or 15/10[Expert Jobs](except mimic he needs 25/10) for first Job Change.
Then proceed on changing jobs to:
Normal Jobs:
Thief - The Default Class in PRM. Has variety of skills, from melee/magic/ranged and passive to increase your Resource management or stat increases such as HP/SP/Flee.
Raider - Physical Bruiser Class. Unique job that focuses on using spears, dealing average damage and high survivability.
Trickster - Physical Bruiser leech based class. has inbuilt Leech from using Scythes. Fire Endow/AutoGuard and 1-2-3 combo playstyle.

Jester - Hybrid Physical/Magical class. Uses Unique Decks of cards that gives different effects depending on suit used. High ASPD limit. Burst and Spam Skills. and strong finisher that consumes HP to deal damage.

Ronin - Physical DPS Class. Excells on High Evade and burst damage with combo skills. Way of the Blade buff increases damage dealt with skills, but lost on taking any damage. Blade Skill Deals Melee damage in combo style. Void Dash skill deals Ranged damage by dashing behind target dealing delayed damage.
Expert Jobs:

Vagabond - Physical DPS class. Deals high dps, with low survivability. Has All element Endows with "Seven Winds". Passsives that increase ASPD/ATK and Flee. Frenzy that sets your APSD to 193 with increased ATK, and disables HP regenration.
Judge - Ranged DPS Class. Has burst damage with skills. High Mobility with Vault skill. Seals Management enables/boosts skills. Has access to variety of Revolvers made in Judge HQ
Dark Knight - Melee/Magic DPS/Bruiser Class. Harvest Buff Removes Regen, but increases Skill damage based on missing health. Black Heart gives 100% leech chance with 10% amount.

Peacekeeper - Melee/Ranged Class. Combo Style Character that has continuous combo gameplay. Damage scaled on dex, and other stats while under crash trinket effect. Trinkets can grant unique effects from Stat Scaling/Buffs/Debuffs.

Illusionist - Magic based Summoner class. Can summon Kimi to assist caster in combat. Uses Unique Gloves to change effect on Real Magic Attack. Grand Summoning can summon up to 5 monster to fight alongside Illusionist.
Mimic - 4fun Class. Can cast all 150 skills in the game depending on RNG with Abracadabra. Plagiarism can Save skill from other classes that he can use manually.
sections.title: First Job Change

paras: Upon Changing to your first Job. You will get "Weapon Voucher" that can be acquired from achievements tab, that can be exchanged for starting job weapon at Ornstein NPC located in backrooms on first floor. Choose weapon depending on what build you are going. it won't last for long time. Expert Jobs such as Judge and Peacekeeper receieves unique Accessory that gives +10% exp/ASPD +3/SP +10 until base level 30.
Now you will probably want to get some job levels. You can level in upper levels of Morroc Pyramids, if its too hard. you can always go back to basement until you level your damaging skills.
After you get your basic skills. its time to finally start the journey to level 130. it won't be an easy road. But remember PRM is Marathon, not a sprint.

Effective Exp from monsters counts by +/- 15 level range, but leveling spots will be listed with preferable player level and +5 of monsters level, Leveling spots will depend on your job/gear and stats, if its too hard, you can always level in easier spot or use reset fountain and spend points in stats that you missing: HP/SP/Damage/Cast Time and etc..
Leveling Spots:
"Morroc Pyramid Basement": 1 ~ 14. Starting leveling spot, you can easily get 10/10 or 15/10 for first job change.

Items to get: Lost Attire shadow Set - First Shadow set. Orphan Cloths set - gives increase exp. Orphan Runes - first orphan runes from first orphan coffer, gives stats like ATK/MATK/HP and SP. Familiar Card - 5 hp recover on physical damage.
"Upper Morroc Pyramid": 5 ~ 25. Minorous/Mummy.
Items to get: Lost Tomb Ring - grants SP on kill great for early game resource management.
"Payon Cave F1/F2/F3": 10 ~ 28 Skeleton Archer/Soldier. Sohee. Nine Tails. Fire Fox.
Items to get: Scarlet set. Legacy of Arrows set for ranged classes. Bone weapons. Moonlight Dagger for Bolters.
"Insect Society": 10 ~ 20. Even tho this dungeon considered low level dungeon. It can be quite rippy for certain jobs and while having low hp and hard DEF. Go here mostly for items.

Items to get: Insect Wings - Movement speed garment. Scaraba Tower - AutoGuard 10 shield with great defences. Quick Swarming shadow set for Variable cast reduction. Carapace Armor For melee classes. Dark Tights for ranged classes. Mother's nightmare ETC items for Insect society Scholar Accessory exchange.
"Prontera culvert F2": 14 ~ 34. Mega Thief Bug/Fulbuk. Good leveling spot especially if you have AoE.
Items to get: Running shoes - high base movement speed shoes, look for Move speed random option. Golden Buckler - good sheild with Regen.
"Geffen Cave entrance map": 20 ~ 35. Goblins.
Items to get: Wooden Mail, Gives large HP bonus for max SP cost, great for Expert Jobs since their hp pool is low, if you can sustain SP.
"Geffen Field 08": 28 ~ 40' Earth/Sky Petite and Wild Rose.
"Geffen Cave": 30 ~ 40 F2-F3. All mobs.
Items to get: Drainliar Card, Bloody Mage card in shield.
"Orc Village": 35 ~ 45. Orc Warrior/Orc Lady/Orc Baby. Good exp. dodge Axe Torando from Orc Warriors if you don't have high hp.
"West Orc Village": 39 ~ 50 High Orc/Orc Archers.
You can also try to kill Orc Lord for Medic Manual X, which gives "Heal" lvl 10.

bullets: Rogue - Hybrid Class with multiple "build" skill tree, depending on skill tree chosen can be Melee Bruiser, Creator or Hunter type classes and also having shield mastery tree. Can further change jobs by getting specialization or Unchained evolution.

Prowler - Melee Dps class. Scales Flee and Perfect Dodge. Improves Backstab from thief skill kit. High Burst damage and evasion. Uses Unique Off-hand.

Shadowseer - Pseudo Melee Magic class. Adds MATK as ATK. Uses Off-hand dagger that increases range(Class is still melee). Depends on Auto spell skil, bursting enemy with autocasting spells. High DPS and ASPD. Squishy.
Unchained Thief - Super Novice of PRM. Unlocks core skills from both Rogue/Assassin classes. Can further Unchain by getting core skills of all Specialization classes.

sections.title: Leveling? I Love it!

bullets: Arcane Master - Unrestricted magic. Gain access to variety of AoE spells and heavy hitting finisher. Tree of Yggdrasil that can revive fallen allies. Comet that Decreases elemental resistances of monster and more.

Kingslayer - Master of Strategy. Chess style character that has Queen's[Mostly Black] and King's skills[Mostly White]. Improves damage with "Left" Skill tree, offering more damaging skills. Improves Defences with "Right" Skill tree, offering defensive buffs and effects. Can use Heavy Finisher that uses total SP by adding spent SP into % ATK.
Blast Juggler - Rules? Explosions are only option. Great AoE and Sustain. Gain more Trap skills and explosions. increases potion effectiveness. And cooked food for caster and allies.

paras: The Night Raven is a master of wielding any combination of weapons. It has access to a high variety of situational skills, that can fill any variety of builds and styles.

sections.title: A true master of all weapons

paras: The Night Raven has no enforced rotation, this gives players full control of the best rotation they can use to improve their damage power. This makes the Night Raven:
A very mobile DPS with multiple hit and run options using all kinds of weapons according to situation, allowing them to quickly dominate unpredictable fights
Due to it's nature in wielding multiple weapons, Most of its offensive skills have varied scaling and deal Boosted Scaling Damage when wielding matching weapons.
The use of the Raven (similar to the original game's Falcon) brings alternative concepts, ensuring a night raven will always have ways to deal reliable damage to enemies, if prepared for it.

Night Raven can also apply a Night Wound to targets. This red cross-shaped debuff provides minor extra damage with most skills when used on a marked target, making Blitz Beat and Blade Dancer's Southern Cross great openers to any rotation. The bonus is also small enough that it doesn't feel punishing for missing or ignoring its window.
Finally, the Night Raven can proc the Raven's attacks automatically when auto-attacking, if the player is wielding specifically a dagger + sword combination.
sections.title: Gameplay Identity

bullets: Double Dagger Builds should always Get Definitive Dagger.
Double Sword Builds should always Get Northern Cross.
Double Axe Builds should always get Bloody Fangs.
Dagger+Sword Builds can have impressive auto attack power with Blitz Beat procs.
All builds should consider Typhoon Edge for AoE coverage if they need it or the Raven Skills for more reliability.
Final Skill: Raven Steps. Requires having a Raven, quickly dashes to any location with a very small cooldown and SP cost.
paras: Final jobs always have varied core loops. The Night Raven is not a very skill point starved job, meaning it doesn't need to get a ton of skills to become decent... as long as you know what you're looking for:
Rest of skill points can be used for buffs, mobility and overall class coverage.

Due to access to Raven Steps to quickly move out of danger, a Night Raven can take bigger risks when fighting strong enemies. This allows them to use longer combo rotations with less risk, mixing Blade Dancer skills like Soul Destroyer and alternating Southern Cross (for it's doubled damage when reused in a short window due to Night Wound) is very recommended to boost the damage potential while rotating the cooldowns quickly.
Overall, the Night Raven is a very free-form job, fitting for players who would rather be creative in their progression and experimenting with varied combinations of skills.

paras: The **Paradox system** introduces a clear separation between different gameplay environments, designed to support **seasonal content** and alternative progression paths without affecting the main game.
At its core, Paradox exists to ensure that progress made in one environment cannot be carried into another. This keeps each experience fair, self-contained, and balanced over time.
Characters and items belong to a specific realm. Interactions are only allowed when both sides belong to the same realm.
In practice, this means that Paradox and Normal gameplay do not mix. Items, zeny, and progression obtained in Paradox cannot be transferred to Normal characters, and vice versa.
This separation helps prevent indirect advantages, same-account transfers, and unintended shortcuts between different progression environments.

Each season represents a fresh, self-contained experience where players can start over, explore new mechanics, and progress through exclusive content.
Paradox characters are the foundation of seasonal gameplay.

paras: Each Paradox season features its own dedicated questlines. These quests are designed to introduce the seasonal theme, guide progression, and encourage exploration of season-specific mechanics.
Seasonal questlines are exclusive to Paradox characters and do not interact with Normal progression.

paras: Seasons use a separate reward system based on **Seasonal Tickets**.
These tickets are earned through Paradox gameplay and can be exchanged for seasonal rewards, cosmetics, and other exclusive items tied to that season.
Seasonal rewards are designed to remain within the Paradox ecosystem and do not affect the Normal economy.
sections.title: Seasonal tickets & rewards

paras: Paradox is not meant to replace the Normal game. It exists as an optional, parallel experience that allows for experimentation, fresh progression, and seasonal content.
By keeping realms isolated, the server can safely introduce new ideas, mechanics, and progression models while preserving the integrity of the core game.

bullets: They are extremely deadly while being hard to counter-react, as long as their SP remains, they will overwhelm any target with quick hits.
paras: The Prowler is a job that focuses on creating opportunities to instantly take down its targets or to dance around them avoiding hits, for this reason:
As Prowlers have very small skill kits, they are straightforward to build. Relying on their special passive skills and Armguards to work in a multitude of ways.

The Thief skill Backstab is the centerpiece of the Prowler's kit. With the boosts from the passives, this skill can activate Combo Ready and receive incredible power boosts, allowing a Prowler to quickly start any combat from any situation in an advantage, ready to follow up in a multitude of ways, usually with Shadowstab.
Another unique tool to the Prowler is the Rope Kunai, a unique weapon that allows a Prowler to pull enemies close by using the Flying Knife skill.
sections.title: Gameplay Identity

paras: A key factor on the Prowler is it's easy access to Perfect Dodge, making attaining even 100% perfect dodge, an easy task for most builds. This may not negate every damage taken, but the almost complete negation of all auto attacks makes them very resistant and virtually unkillable if correctly played.

Most times, a Prowler will use Backstab to close-in on enemies and follow up with Shadowstab for as long as the Combo Ready window allows. This makes building both SP, SP regen and ASPD essential for the Prowler in order to not run out of energy for the barrage of skills.

Rope Kunai can be used to bring enemies that are out of reach, increasing the overall fighting speed. Whirling Kunai is a very strong, short range (but still ranged) damage skill that allows for heavy damage in an area, Even with a long cooldown, it's a reliable and strong tool to fit into rotations.
Macabre is a powerful buff that increases the overall fighting capacity of the Prowler for a duration by consuming HP, being a great risk-rewards mechanic to play around.
The multiple evasive skills of the Prowler can be used to greatly reduce damage for the specific cases where they are needed.

paras: The Raider is the opposite of the Trickster. It's a safe job class that can progress at a steady pace and handle most situations, making this job:
A well rounded warrior with good damage variety, high frontline potential and a simple kit that can cover every situation it faces.

A smart Raider knows what path to take to correctly engage enemies. In risky situations they may favor the use of a 1-Handed Spear with a Shield to keep the enemies at bay. When more comfortable they can swap into the powerful 2-Handed Wyrm Spear to increase their damage potential and Dragon Thrust Level.
Dragon Thrust is a Powerful Opener for the Dracomancer. The level of this skill that is enabled depends on the currently equipped spear. The skill is the center-piece of any Raider or Dracomancer.
The entire kit of a Raider is built around skills that should be used situationally, either by pushing enemies back, increasing defenses or attacking with more offensive power.

Raiders have quick job level growth, hitting the max Job level of 50 well before most other non-thief jobs. However, only the best will be able to continue their training until they peak and become a Dracomancer.

bullets: Rank E dungeons usually are recommended for players who are not used to the combat mechanics of Return to Morroc.
Rank E dungeon have difficulty similar or slightly below fields.
Rank E mechanics usually are easy to predict, avoidable, require no specific gears and rarely have potential to one shot on major mistakes.
paras: Rank E dungeons are very easy overall. They are meant for players that don't want to stress over long fights and want an easier time. This doesn't mean they are boring or don't have mechanics, they can still hurt those unprepared.
Recommendations
Party: Any party with any level of preparation.
Solo: Any player with any level of preparation.
sections.title: RANK E

bullets: Rank D dungeons usually are recommended for players who understand basic mechanics of Return to Morroc.
Rank D dungeon have difficulty slightly above fields.
Rank D mechanics usually are reasonable to predict, avoidable, require no specific gears and have very minor potential to one shot. Monsters may have minor combo sequences.
paras: Rank D dungeons require attention and managing resources to farm effectively. They can still be handled with basic gear, but mistakes are more punishing and luring too many monsters can prove fatal.
Recommendations
Party: Any party with any level of preparation. A party of 2+ is recommended for ungeared parties.
Solo: Any player with basic level of preparation. Access to Heal Lv5 is greatly recommended.
sections.title: RANK D

bullets: Rank C dungeons usually are recommended for players who know the skill mechanics of Return to Morroc.
Rank C dungeon monsters may have multiple patterns/mechanics.
Rank C mechanics usually are predictable, avoidable, require no specific gears and have minor potential to one shot. Monsters may have minor combo sequences and reactive skills under specific cases.
paras: Rank C dungeons can hurt unprepared players. They usually require basic cards or reactions based on enemy behavior. They can still be handled when undergeared but they may provide a challenge and mistakes can be crippling.
Recommendations
Party: Any party with basic level of preparation. A party of 3+ is recommended for ungeared parties.
Solo: Any player with cards and reasonable level of preparation. Access to Heal Lv5 is greatly recommended.
sections.title: RANK C

bullets: Rank B dungeons usually are recommended for players who are very comfortable with the combat of Return to Morroc.
Rank B dungeon monsters have varied engaging ways, may disrupt player actions and apply status effects.

Rank B mechanics are predictable and avoidable, but require precision. They require moderate gear and have some potential for one shots when damage is ignored. Monsters may have combo sequences, reactive skills and disruptions such as status effects and movement impairment.
paras: Rank B dungeons are always a challenge when a player is on the same level range. They require reasonable cards and knowing the job potential and limits. Monsters usually require multiple rotations to be killed and can force the player to fight under their rules in specific cases.
Recommendations
Party: Any party with cards and good level of preparation. A party of 5+ is recommended for undergeared parties. Not recommended for ungeared parties.
Solo: Any player with good cards and decent level of preparation. Access to Heal Lv10 is greatly recommended.
sections.title: RANK B

bullets: Rank A dungeons are recommended only for players who are very comfortable and understand the combat of Return to Morroc.
Rank A dungeon monsters have multiple mechanics, minor phase changes and react in unpredictable ways.

Rank A mechanics are both avoidable and precise. Monsters may include unavoidable mechanics to act as checks for resistances, prediction and defenses under specific cases. Monsters may have specific status immunities or knockback resistances.
paras: Rank A dungeons are harder dungeons that have small margin for error. They punish players for any mistakes and in some cases can be fatal. Cards and refined gear are regular needs, along with status resistances. A player who is not prepared may fight for some time, but death is sure to come eventually.
Recommendations
Party: Prepared party with cards and decent equipment. A party of 4+ is recommended for mid-geared parties. Not recommended for undergeared parties.
Solo: Any player with good cards and decent level of preparation. Access to Heal Lv10 is greatly recommended.
sections.title: RANK A

bullets: Rank S dungeons are recommended only for players who mastered the combat of Return to Morroc.

Rank S dungeon monsters have multiple mechanics, aggression and can be unpredictable. They can use skills under new rules, have specific counters to specific combat methods or require strong mitigation or some equip swapping.

Rank S mechanics can be split in multiple parts, ensuring a player needs to pay attention to what a monster already did to know what to expect. Monsters may change behavior and require careful positioning during the fight so as not to kill a party member as colateral damage while handling a skill.
Mistakes can be punished with one shots or even party wipes.
paras: Rank S dungeons are among the hardest challenges in Return to Morroc. They can take down even prepared parties with a barrage of skills, status, monsters and phases. They are always punishing and failing a very clear, very obvious long mechanic pretty much guarantees death.
Recommendations
Party: Prepared party with good cards and good equipment. A party of 6 is recommended for mid-geared parties. Not recommended for low-geared parties.
Solo: A very well prepared and experient player. Access to Heal Lv10 is required for any chance of success.

In Return to Morroc when an equipment fails a refinement, you no longer lose the item, it just downgrades. This ensures any item can be refined anytime without the risk of losing hours upon hours of progress.

On the other hand, some items might require more resources to properly refine. Higher refinement levels require better Ores, even if sometimes it may seem like the costs are not that great, it DOES make it harder than usual.
With this, you can always refine an item and get some extra bonuses to help you, and save your resources for that one item that you really believe is worth to refine to the highest level.
It's important to mention the Refinement System is entirely ingame, with no cash shop or pay-to-win at all.
Maximum refine rate is +10.
sections.title: No Losses

paras: The Refine Materials in Return to Morroc are based on the item refine level, not on how they behave.
Oridecon: Used for Weapons
Elunium: Used for Armors
The materials above come in four versions:
Regular: Used to refine from +0 to +3
HD: Used to refine from +4 to +6
Enriched: Used to refine from +7 to +9
Jewel: Used to refine to +10
Players can use an item from a higher tier to refine without risk of downgrade on lower tiers.
however this costs twice as much zeny as it would normally.
Example:
Upgrading a Weapon to +3 can be done with a HD Oridecon, if it fails, it won't downgrade the item.
Doing this with an unimproved weapon will let it improve to +1 guaranteed.
Runes and Shadow Items also have their own materials:
Shadowdecons: Used for Shadow Items
Bradium: Used for Runes
They also can use Jewel Shadowdecons and Jewel Bradiums, needed for refining to +10, to prevent downgrades up to +9.
sections.title: Refine Materials

paras: The bonuses from refining equipment is different from other servers.
Armor: For each +2, increase the DEF provided by the equipment by 1.
Weapon: For each +1, increase the ATK and MATK provided by the weapon by 0.5 per Level of the weapon
This means that you only see an increase in ATK for Level 1 Weapons for each +2 of refinement.
Shadow Armor and Runes: Benefit is dependent on the specific piece of gear. Some shadow armor refinement bonuses require you to be using the entire set, so read carefully before you refine.

paras: The Rune System is a unique system for Return to Morroc.
Runes have powerful bonuses. These bonuses can be improved by refining the runes. A rune is harder to refine than a common equipment.
The runes also change the color of your character when equipped. So it's also a strategic element, as for example, Wearing a fire damage boosting rune, will change one's color to red.
Runes can be obtained in a variety of ways.
Neutral Rune: Simple runes that can't be refined, can be used at any level and provide minor bonuses, perfect for beginners.
White Rune: Runes with unique variations that change the way you can engage content.
Dark Rune: Job Runes. They improve specific skills and stats of the job they belong to. Only one per job is available.
Purple Rune: Power Runes. Improve overall mechanical performance of the wearer.
Orange Rune: Growth Runes. Helps the wearer grow and evolve faster in a variety of ways.
Green Rune: Guard Runes. improves general defensive powers of the wearer.
Blue Rune: Elemental Runes. Boost power and resistances to certain elements.
Special Rune: Unique Runes. provide unique properties that can't be obtained anywhere else.

paras: The Satsujin can handle any fight in any situation due to its high variety of skills, this makes them:
A reliable fighter that has the tools for any situation and any difficulty, being the most adaptable job among all.

With the high variety of skill types, building for a Satsujin under a single "style" is not recommended. A good Satsujin will know what they need to excel in any combat situation using their multitude of tools.

Wielding the Shinobi skills with a new concept, the change of elements, change of attack types and change of combat situations constantly put the Satsujin in a very privileged position against an enemy that might be impossible for someone else to fight.
The difference between a mediocre Satsujin and a great Satsujin is very easy to see during combat due to how they can make their skills synergize or not.

paras: The Shadowseer is a spellblade job, which uses multiple enchantments to deal magic damage and cast spells along with auto attacks.
The amount of continuous magic damage is unmatched by any other job, especially when properly played.
sections.title: Watcher of Light and Darkness

paras: The Shadowseer is a job that brings out the strongest forms of autospell available, making them capable of causing a flurry of magic damage with supportive physical damage, raining down spells with extremely fast power while keeping balance of its buffs.
While Shadowseers in fighting are very simple jobs, their true difficulty comes in the maintenance of its enchantments, since most of them have harsh SP % costs and very long cast times.

The correct use of Equinox is essential, as it removes most of the cast time of its spells, with the downside of requiring an enemy target to cast, forcing it to be used under a combat scenario. The Shadowseer can opt to slowcast its buffs and enchantments outside combat, at the cost of harsh cast times.
The Shadowseer also has a unique tool in Astral Mastery which converts its MATK into raw ATK, only during auto-attacks, allowing its magic damage to effectively become critical hits on some builds.

The Offhand Dagger is a unique secondary tool that provides them with higher levels of Double Attack regardless of main weapon, at the cost of not providing auto-attacks. This weapon has multiple interactions with the Masteries of the job, especially Spectral Mastery.
sections.title: Gameplay Identity

paras: The Shadowseer has a very different gameplay loop from most jobs. While they will usually rotate skills actively during combat, the Shadowseer will rotate its cast times for enchants and buffs in preparation and only after that, it can begin fighting enemies to the best of its abilities.

The use of Convention while very risky due to heavy costs, is also a strong tool to fight, as under specific circumstances, allows thief magic to be always autocast at Lv10, breaking the usual restriction of randomly using Lv1~5.

Umbral Cut is the definitive finisher of the job. Dealing massive damage, it requires long setups and procs of spirit spheres from Astral Weapon. The spheres have a short duration, forcing the Shadowseer to always be on the offensive in order to finally summon enough spheres for the cast of a strong, large AoE Umbral Cut.

By finding a correct balance between speed, power, magic, physical damage and magical damage, the Shadowseer can attack an enemy with excellent reliability, proving to be one of the hardest, and most rewarding, jobs in Return to Morroc.

paras: The Sinner is a safe fighter that can take down enemies either with a strong precise hit or a barrage of many arrows.
Due to their incredible use of Bows, Sinners can take down enemies before they become a threat with the correct balance of positioning, power and resources.
sections.title: Raining death from afar

paras: The Sinner can be built around two extremely different play styles, both of them are very good in handling combat situations and requiring positioning, so they:
Can adapt to difficult situations and tackle challenges much above what other jobs would consider doable by themselves, but requiring perfect balance of gameplay.

The Sinner can use a multitude of tools at their disposal to always keep their SP ready to spend, this is paramount in their gameplay since the high consumption of the skills can quickly render them useless if not well planned.

Due to being able to quickly setup turrets around, the Sinner can cover an area with constant damage while focusing on avoiding damage and repositioning, using Decoy from Rogue is a core skill that will quickly differentiate the greatest Sinners from the rest.

If a Sinner is allowed to fully prepare before a fight, they can end it all with a single attack by using Final Arrow, by stacking as many buffs as possible and along with Inquisition Resolve, potentially dealing the strongest direct hit in the game (with some luck).
